title_en: Carmela the Different 5 - I Want to Find Langlang

full_text_zh:
[P1] 不一样的卡梅拉
亚马逊网站五星级童书
★★★★★
我要找到朗朗
〔法〕克利斯提昂·约里波瓦/文 〔法〕克利斯提昂·艾利施/图
郑迪蔚/译
二十一世纪出版社

[P2] 这天晚上，鸡舍里的小鸡们躁动得像一群跳蚤。卡梅利多、小胖墩、小刺头、软耳朵和他的伙伴们闹鬼般叫嚷着。而小卡门则和她的伙伴们安安静静地、乖乖地坐在那里。激动的时刻到了，所有的小鸡们都盯着大门不动。因为今天是星期一！
而星期一将会有……
咯！咯！咯！

[P3] “晚上好，小鸡们！”
“晚上好，故事爷爷！”小鸡们争先恐后地说。
故事爷爷刚一坐下，小鸡们就都闭上了嘴，安静得都能听到羽毛落地的声音。周一讲故事的时间到啦！
“嗯！嗯！”
故事爷爷清了清嗓子，开始念起了魔法咒语：
“空特……空德……空提……空达！大的小的都竖起耳朵吧。
空特……空德……空提……空达！我那神奇口袋打开啦。
故事马上就要开始啦……”

[P4] 小鸡们先津津有味地听了列那狐的传奇故事……
接着是尤利西斯战胜……
独眼巨人的故事……
还有他们听了一百遍也不会厌烦的“金鸡蛋”的故事。

[P5] 时间过得真快。大家都希望永远沉浸在这么美好的时光中，但是……

“空特……空德……空提……空达！是关上神奇口袋的时间啦！今天晚上就到这儿吧。”
“啊，这么快！”小鸡们抗议道……

卡门和卡梅利多赶紧跑上前：“给你，这是我们画的画。”

“谢谢，我的小鸡们。”故事爷爷非常感动，“现在我要走了，我还得赶到山顶上的鸡舍去。”
“再见了，故事爷爷！”

“下周一，一定要再来啊！”卡梅利多喊道。

[P6] 小鸡们扫兴地准备乖乖回窝睡觉。
“嗨！看，故事爷爷忘了带他的奶酪口袋了。”
卡门喊道。

“你在吃什么呢，贝里奥？”卡梅利多问道。
“嗯嗯！”小白羊有些不自在地回答道。

“一块用上好的羊奶做的奶酪……我实在有点忍不住了！”贝里奥供认不讳。

苍白的月光下，故事爷爷迈着细碎而沉重的脚步渐渐走远。他喘着气，关节咔咔作响，他已经快走不动了。

“我怎么越来越老啦！”他悲叹道，“我承受不了鸡舍间的奔波了，我已经筋疲力尽。”
他有了个悲观的念头：“如果我不在了，谁来给孩子们讲故事？”

[P7] 卡梅利多、卡门和贝里奥赶紧带着奶酪口袋追了出去。
“他应该走得不远！”
“嘘！你们听……”
“好像是哭泣声。”卡梅利多惊讶地说，“真不敢相信！是故事爷爷在哭啊！”
“哦……不至于吧！”贝里奥说，“就为了块奶酪，不至于吧！”
“哦，是你们呀？”这位走街串巷的故事大师用衣袖擦了擦鼻涕，颤抖着问。
“你怎么啦？”卡门不安地问道。
“孩子们，我老啦……太老了！快要到去天堂见故事家族的祖先的时候了……”
呜呜呜！！
“……我实在太累了，到现在还没有找到接班人。”故事爷爷号啕大哭起来。

[P8] 突然，一股强大的气流
从井底喷出来！

“现在是哭的时候吗！
“哦！是您吗，伊索叔叔？！”故事爷爷喊道。
“别害怕，朋友们，是我叔叔！他是他那个时代
最著名的故事大王，好多我们熟悉的寓言都是伊
索叔叔教我的。”

“你说什么来着，我的孩子？你一直没有
找到继承者？！”鬼魂用低沉的声音问道，“这
可太糟糕了！回答我，你还记得那个能让你
找到继承者的预言吗？”

“你的继承者叫朗朗，你会发现他睡在叶子
上，你必须跟着箭头去找他。”

[P9] “我跟随过很多箭头，找了
很多地方！树林、乡村、山谷……
叔叔，但我从来都没有找到那个
睡在叶子上的神秘的朗朗……”

“时间越来越紧迫了，我的侄子！如果你在三天内没
有找到继承者，我们的故事将会被遗忘！”
“还剩下三天的时间来完成这项工作！三天，我的侄
子！你听清了吗？！”

“三天！！！”

“我愿意全身心地来学习这些故事，真的，
我太喜欢讲故事了！”卡梅利多建议道。
“唉，我的孩子，预言是明确的！一定要找
到那个朗朗来继承我。”

“朗朗，我就认识十几个呢！”卡门突然喊道，
“我们一起来帮你找吧！”

[P10] 说干就干！天一亮，大家就上路了。故事爷爷再也没有力气走路了，只能由贝里奥一路背着。
“跟着箭头走！”卡门提议道。
“箭头？在哪儿？”贝里奥边找边说。

“能告诉我你讲的那些故事都是从哪儿来的吗？”卡梅利多问。

“当然有一些是我想象出来的！”趴在背上的故事爷爷咯咯笑道，“绝大多数的故事是继承来的。从最早的时候起，它们便由故事家族一代代传下来，这是一笔财富呀！”

[P11] 寻找者们首先来到著名的短跑运动健将长耳朵朗朗的家，因为他的耳朵，人们给了他一个绰号叫“箭头”。

“啊，你们是谁？看样子你们好像要对我说什么事情……
再告诉我一下你们的名字？”兔子没头没脑地说了一大堆话。
“朗朗！是我们！卡门和卡梅利多！”

卡梅利多向他解释了一大早来访的目的。
“成为‘说书的’！”野兔大声喊道，“太好了！而且我会学得
很快！速度是我的专长！我们现在开始……开始吗？”

但是结果，野兔朗朗根本记不住哪怕一个故事，就算重复很多次也不行。
“等一下！等一下！我要这样才能记得住，我
保证，看！为了不忘记我把耳朵打个结。”

三个小伙伴看到这一幕，使劲捂着嘴不让自己
笑出声来。
“耳朵上打的结多像‘大麻花’，可怜的家伙！”
大家终于忍不住笑翻在草丛中。

哈！
哈！
哈！

[P12] “显然，野兔朗朗不是那个预言里说的朗朗。”
“别泄气。”卡门说，“我们再去找别的睡在叶子上的朗朗。”

“朋友们你们这就快要走了吗？真遗憾，
我们玩得多开心……嗯……我们刚才玩了
什么来着？”

大伙儿接着又去找了狼朗朗、猞猁朗朗和
蜥蜴朗朗，但都不是他们要找的那位。
“我快背不动故事爷爷了！”贝里奥嘟囔
着说，“最好能尽快想个好办法。”

富有创意的卡门想了一晚，终于想出这
个抬椅子的办法。第二天，大家又出发了。
“今天咱们去找谁？”故事爷爷问道。
“去找这个山洞的主人。”卡梅利多回答
道，“他是这个地区最恶心的家伙，一个真正
的恐怖分子！”

“看哪！”贝里奥吓得脸色苍白，“这儿有
尸骨!!! 我……我 还是 在这儿 等你们吧！”

[P13] 冒着被蝙蝠攻击的危险，卡梅利多、卡门和故事爷爷摸索着向山洞深处走去。突然，他们来到了一个洞穴……
“嗨！嗨！
狗熊朗朗？你醒醒呀！”

[P14] “啊——嗯——啊!!!”
“谁那么大胆敢打扰我睡觉?! 这已经是第二次吵醒我了!”狗熊朗朗说,“但愿你们能有个很好的理由……否则我的脾气可不怎么好!!!”

“一个箭头!就像预言里说的……难道真的是他?!”

在卡梅利多的鼓励下,
故事爷爷将此行的目的说了出来:

“朗朗先生,您……您有没有想过换一个职业?比如说成……成为说书人?”

啊!

[P15] “是你弄疼我的吗，小不点？！”狗熊朗朗大发雷霆，“嗯！我要将你……”

“安静点，大胖熊！看这个！是我从你屁股上拔出来的！”

“啊！难怪我睡不好觉！”狗熊朗朗嘟嘟囔囔地说，“谢谢你啊，小鸡。这个箭头是一个小孩的，他家在喷泉附近。昨天，这个小坏蛋拿他的玩具弓箭威胁我……”

趁着狗熊朗朗转变了态度，故事爷爷赶紧再次提出请求：“你愿意接我的班吗，朗朗先生？”

“我感到很荣幸！”狗熊朗朗大声说道，“可是这样工作量很大！我每年还要冬眠六个月呢！唔，晚安吧！”

“呼噜呼噜……”

[P16] 第二个晚上就要结束了，尽管他们找了很久地方，走遍了山川河谷，但自始至终没有见到预言中的朗朗。大家都有点筋疲力尽、疲惫不堪了。

只有卡门独自花了大半夜的时间，想出一个比抬椅子走更好的办法，既便捷又省力。
“嗯！得找到一个能转的东西，有了……辘轳！”

只剩最后一天了！
他们决定去桦树林里的白鼬的家。
“看到了吧，这个朗朗有个臭哄哄的秘密巢穴！”
卡梅利多喊道。
“我闻着还挺好的嘛！”卡门咯咯地笑着。

与此同时，在农场里。
“啊？谁拿走了我的辘轳？！我现在该怎么打水呀？！”

[P17] 浑身散发着“香气”的白鼬在他的洞口等着他们。
“是什么好风一大早就把你们吹来了？”
“我在找一个朗朗，他将要替代我来给大家讲故事。”
“我的妈呀，这是什么味儿！”卡梅利多和卡门几乎快要
晕倒了。

“不用再找了！”臭气冲天的白鼬朗朗兴奋地
说，“我就是你们要找的那个朗朗！”

故事爷爷深深呼吸了一大口新鲜空气后，
才勉强鼓起勇气去赞赏白鼬。但是依旧受不了那
股臭味，过了一会儿，他终于晕倒在地。

“谁能给我解释一下，为什么他不能
胜任这项工作？”贝里奥问。

美树林

[P18] 他们不知疲倦地问遍了这里所有叫朗朗的家伙。
“接替故事爷爷？对不起，我还没有结束疗养呢！”
“说书？这我挺有兴趣的，但是我正在等
一位公主的亲吻呢！”
“你怎么敢对像我
这么正直的獾提出这
种问题！！！”
“嗨……请问？”
“忙着呢！！！”
“哦，这几个家伙连
问都不要问！”

[P19] 第三天晚上，一切都该结束了。
卡门、卡梅利多和贝里奥感到十分沮丧！
他们最后一个访问的是猫头鹰朗朗。
它住在市政府的钟楼里。
唉！漂亮的猫头鹰也不是他们要找的朗朗。
故事爷爷坐着沉默无语，太失败了！他即将要去
另一个世界了，故事家族的财富将失传了。

突然，卡梅利多惊奇地发现……

“看那里！一支箭钉在木窗上！一个箭头！”
“兄弟们看好啦！”卡门喊道，“我认出来了，这支
箭和上回射中狗熊朗朗屁股的那支是一样的！”
“好兆头！”卡梅利多说，“跟我来！”

“贝里奥！过来帮帮我们！”小鸡们大声喊。

[P20] “以小鸡的名义!!!”
卡门喊道：“我敢打赌这就是
那个狗熊朗朗提到的小男孩！你们
知道吗？他正睡在人们称它为
‘纸’的叶子上呀!!!”

没有时间再胡乱猜测了，他们跑进了屋子。
“请问？”卡梅利多问道，“你叫什么名字？”

[P21] 小男孩被吵醒了，很惊奇地看着这几位到访者。
“嗯……朗朗！”男孩回答道。
“你喜欢讲故事吗，我的小朗朗？”故事爷爷紧张得心怦怦直跳。
“哦，是啊，非常喜欢！特别是关于小动物的故事。”小男孩开朗地笑道。
“嗨，听着！谢谢你们把我叫醒，我在写检讨时睡着了，要写一百遍——
‘我再也不在教室里学狗熊叫逗同学们笑了’。”
“还有更紧急的事情！”故事爷爷说，“我的小朗朗，你愿意成为……故事的继承者吗？”
“哦，我不知道是不是能够……”
“很简单！我会给你讲许多故事，你都要牢记在心。”
“我愿意试试！”
故事爷爷太激动了。高兴地看着眼前这位继承者，他清了清嗓子。
“空特……空德……空提……
空达！大的小的都竖起耳朵吧。
空特……空德……空提……空达！我那神奇口袋打开了。
故事就从这里开始吧……”

[P22] 一直到天亮，故事爷爷讲啊，讲啊，讲啊……
寓言、童话、神话、传奇故事源源不断地从他嘴里像泉水一样涌出。
小男孩也很认真，不落一字地记录着这些故事。
刷，刷，刷，羽毛笔在纸上飞快地写着。

故事爷爷首先给他讲的是伊索寓言。
“我太喜欢这些故事了！”小朗朗兴奋地说，
“您知道我要做什么吗？嗯……为了不忘掉这些
故事，我决定把它们都写下来！”

任务完成了，卡梅利多、卡门和贝里奥放心地睡着了。

[P23] 一个月以后，让小鸡们
激动的时间又到了，他们全
都紧盯着大门。

没有什么好奇怪的，
因为今天是星期一。

星期一……

咚！咚！咚！

[P24] “晚上好，朋友们！
今天的晚会，首先我要给大家讲一段森林
里的歌唱家、奶酪爱好者受骗的故事！”

这就是……
乌鸦与狐狸……
full_text_en:
[P1] Different Chicken Camille
Amazon's Five-Star Children's Book
★★★★★
I Want to Find Langlang
[France] Christian Jolibois / Text [France] Christian Heinrich / Illustrations
Zheng Diwei / Translator
21st Century Publishing House

[P2] This evening, the chicks in the coop were restless like a group of fleas. Camille, Fatso, Spiky, Soft Ears, and their companions were shouting like ghosts. But little Carmen and her friends sat quietly and obediently. The exciting moment had arrived—every chick was staring at the door. Because today is Monday!
And Monday will bring……
Cluck! Cluck! Cluck!

[P3] "Good evening, little chicks!"
"Good evening, Story Grandpa!" the chicks said eagerly.
As soon as Story Grandpa sat down, the chicks all fell silent, so quiet you could hear a feather fall. It's Monday story time!
"Hmm! Hmm!"
Story Grandpa cleared his throat and began reciting the magic spell:
"Kongte... Kongde... Kongti... Kongda! Big and small, all ears up!
Kongte... Kongde... Kongti... Kongda! My magical pocket is opening now.
The story is about to begin..."

[P4] The chicks first listened with great interest to the legendary tale of Reynard the Fox...
Then came the story of Ulysses defeating...
the one-eyed giant...
And also the story of the 'golden eggs' that they never got tired of hearing, even after a hundred times.

[P5] Time flies. Everyone hopes to stay immersed in this wonderful moment forever, but...

"Kongte... Kongde... Kongti... Kongda! It's time to close the magic pocket! Let's call it a night!"
"Oh, already?" the chicks protested...

Carmen and Caramel rushed forward: "Here, these are the pictures we drew."

"Thank you, my little chicks," the Story Grandpa said, deeply moved. "Now I must go. I still need to get to the chicken coop on top of the mountain."
"Goodbye, Story Grandpa!"

"Next Monday, you must come back!" Caramel shouted.

[P6] The chicks were disappointedly preparing to go back to their nests to sleep.
"Hey! Look, Story Grandpa forgot to bring his cheese bag!" cried Carmen.

"What are you eating, Bélier?" asked Camille.
"Umm..." the little white sheep answered a bit awkwardly.

"A piece of cheese made with fine sheep's milk... I just couldn't resist!" Bélier confessed.

Under the pale moonlight, Story Grandpa walked away with small, heavy steps. He was panting, his joints creaking, and he could hardly move anymore.

"Why am I getting so old!" he sighed, "I can't bear the奔波 between the chicken coops anymore, I'm completely exhausted."
He had a pessimistic thought: "If I'm not here anymore, who will tell stories to the children?"

[P7] Caramelito, Carmen, and Béria quickly ran out with the cheese pocket.
“He can’t be far!”
“Shh! Listen…”
“It sounds like crying,” Caramelito said in surprise. “I can’t believe it! It’s Grandpa Storyteller crying!”
“Oh… it can’t be that bad!” Béria said. “For a piece of cheese? It’s not that serious!”
“Oh, it’s you three?” the wandering storyteller asked, trembling, as he wiped his nose with his sleeve.
“What’s wrong?” Carmen asked anxiously.
“Children, I’m old… too old! It’s almost time to go to heaven to meet the ancestors of the storytelling family…”
Wah wah wah!!
“…I’m just too tired. I still haven’t found a successor.” Grandpa Storyteller sobbed loudly.

[P8] Suddenly, a powerful gust of air
burst from the bottom of the well!

"Is this the time to cry!"
"Oh! Is that you, Uncle Aesop?!" cried Grandpa Storyteller.
"Don't be afraid, friends, it's my uncle! He was the most famous storyteller of his time, and many of the fables we know were taught to us by Uncle Aesop."

"What did you say, my child? You've never found
a successor?!" the ghost asked in a deep voice, "This
is terrible! Answer me, do you still remember the prophecy that can lead you
to your successor?"

"Your successor is named Langlang. You'll find him sleeping on a leaf.
You must follow the arrow to find him."

[P9] "I've followed many arrows, searched
many places! Forests, villages, valleys...
Uncle, but I've never found that
mysterious Langlang sleeping on a leaf..."

"Time is running out, my nephew! If you don't find
an heir within three days, our stories will be forgotten!"
"Only three days left to complete this task! Three days, my nephew!
Did you hear me?!"

"Three days!!!"

"I'm willing to devote myself fully to learning these stories, really,
I love telling stories so much!" suggested Camille.
"Ah, my child, the prophecy is clear! We must find
that Langlang to inherit me."

"Langlang? I know dozens of them!" cried Carmen suddenly,
"Let's help you find him together!"

[P10] Let's get started! As soon as it was light, everyone set off. The Story Grandpa had no strength left to walk, so he had to be carried all the way by Bérenger.
"Follow the arrows!" suggested Carmen.
"Arrows? Where?" Bérenger asked, searching around.

"Can you tell me where all those stories you told came from?" asked Camille.

"Of course, some of them are things I imagined!" chuckled the Story Grandpa, lying on his back. "Most stories are inherited. Since the earliest times, they've been passed down from generation to generation by the Story Family. It's a treasure!"

[P11] The seekers first arrived at the home of the famous sprinter, Long-Eared Langlang, who was nicknamed 'Arrow' because of his long ears.

"Ah, who are you? It seems you want to tell me something... 
Please tell me your names again?" the rabbit blurted out a long string of words.
"Langlang! It's us! Carmen and Camille!"

Camille explained the purpose of their early morning visit.
"Become a 'storyteller'!" the hare shouted excitedly, "Wonderful! And I'll learn it 
very quickly! Speed is my specialty! Shall we begin... begin now?"

But the result was that the hare Langlang simply couldn't remember even a single story, no matter how many times it was repeated.
"Wait! Wait! I need to do this to remember, I 
promise, look! To make sure I don't forget, I'll tie a knot in my ear."

The three companions saw this and struggled to suppress their laughter.
"The knot on his ear looks like a 'big twisty bun', poor fellow!"
Everyone finally burst into laughter in the grass.

Ha!
Ha!
Ha!

[P12] "Clearly, the rabbit Langlang is not the Langlang mentioned in the prophecy."
"Don't lose heart," said Carmen, "let's go find another Langlang sleeping on a leaf."

"Friends, are you really leaving already? What a shame,
we were having such fun... um... what were we just playing?

The group then went on to look for Wolf Langlang, Lynx Langlang, and
Lizard Langlang, but none of them were the one they were seeking.
"I'm almost too tired to carry Story Grandpa anymore!" grumbled Bélier, 
"We should think of a good solution as soon as possible."

Carmen, full of creativity, thought hard all night and finally came up with
this chair-carrying idea. The next day, everyone set off again.
"Who are we going to look for today?" asked Story Grandpa.
"Let's find the owner of this cave," replied Camille, 
"He's the most disgusting creature in this area, a real
terrorist!"

"Look!" Bélier cried, turning pale with fear, "There are
bones here!!! I... I'll just wait here for you!"

[P13] Facing the danger of being attacked by bats, Camille, Carmen, and Grandpa Story cautiously made their way deeper into the cave. Suddenly, they arrived at a cave...
"Hey! Hey!
Bear Langlang? Wake up!"

[P14] "Ah—uh—ah!!!"
"Who dares to disturb my sleep?! This is the second time you've woken me up!" the bear, Langlang, said, "I hope you have a very good reason... otherwise my temper won't be very nice!!!"

"An arrow! Just like in the prophecy... Could it really be him?!"

Encouraged by Camille, the Story Grandfather revealed the purpose of their journey:

"Mr. Langlang, you... have you ever thought about changing careers? For example, becoming... a storyteller?"

Ah!

[P15] "Did you hurt me, little one?!" the bear Langlang roared angrily, "Hmph! I'm going to..."

"Quiet, big fat bear! Look at this! I pulled it out of your butt!"

"Ah! No wonder I couldn't sleep!" Langlang the bear mumbled, "Thank you, little chicken. This arrow belongs to a child, who lives near the fountain. Yesterday, that little rascal threatened me with his toy bow and arrow..."

Seeing that Langlang had changed his attitude, Story Grandpa quickly made his request again: "Would you be willing to take my place, Mr. Langlang?"

"I feel very honored!" Langlang the bear shouted, "But this job is so demanding! I still have to hibernate for six months every year! Hmm, good night!"

"Snore snore..."

[P16] The second night was coming to an end. Despite searching many places and traversing mountains and valleys, they had still not found the prophesied Langlang. Everyone was feeling exhausted and worn out.

Only Carmen spent the entire night alone, thinking of a better way than carrying the chair, one that was both convenient and efficient.
"Hmm! I need to find something that can turn. Got it... a well windlass!"

Only one day left!
They decided to go to the weasel's home in the birch forest.
"Look, this Langlang has a stinky secret den!" cried Camille.
"I think it smells pretty good!" giggled Carmen.

Meanwhile, on the farm.
"What? Who took my well windlass?! How am I supposed to draw water now?!"

[P17] The stinky weasel, reeking of 'aroma', was waiting for them at his cave entrance.
"What a nice breeze brought you all here so early?"
"I'm looking for a Langlang who will replace me to tell stories to everyone."
"Oh my goodness, what is this smell!" Camille and Carmen were almost about to faint.

"No need to look any further!" the stinky weasel Langlang excitedly said, "I am the Langlang you're looking for!"

After taking a deep breath of fresh air, Story Grandpa mustered up the courage to praise the weasel. But he still couldn't stand the smell, and after a while, he finally fainted.

"Who can explain to me why he can't
handle this job?" Berio asked.

Beautiful Forest

[P18] They tirelessly asked every creature here named Langlang.
"Take over from Story Grandpa? Sorry, I haven't finished my recovery yet!"
"Storytelling? I'm quite interested, but I'm waiting for
a princess's kiss!"
"How dare you ask such a question to a
honest badger like me!!!"
"Hi... may I ask?"
"Busy!!!"
"Oh, don't even bother asking these guys!"

[P19] On the third night, everything was supposed to be over.
Carmen, Camille, and Bélier felt very discouraged!
Their last visit was to the owl Langlang.
It lived in the clock tower of the city hall.
Alas! The beautiful owl wasn't the Langlang they were looking for.
The Story Grandfather sat in silence, too defeated! He was about to go
to another world, and the wealth of the Story family would be lost.

Suddenly, Camille discovered something surprising...

"Look there! An arrow stuck in the wooden window! An arrowhead!"
"Brothers, take a good look!" Carmen shouted, "I recognize it—this
arrow is the same one that hit the bear Langlang in the butt last time!"
"Good omen!" Camille said, "Follow me!"

"Bélier! Come help us!" the chicks shouted loudly.

[P20] "In the name of the chicks!!!"
Kamen shouted: "I bet this is the little boy the bear Langlang mentioned! Do you know? He's sleeping on what people call 'paper' leaves!!!"

There was no time for more guessing. They ran into the house.
"Excuse me?" asked Camiludo, "What's your name?"

[P21] The little boy woke up, surprised to see these visitors.
"Hmm... Langlang!" the boy replied.
"Do you like telling stories, my little Langlang?" Story Grandpa's heart pounded with nervousness.
"Oh, yes, I really like it! Especially stories about little animals," the boy laughed cheerfully.
"Hey, listen! Thank you for waking me up. I fell asleep while writing a hundred copies of this—
‘I will never again imitate the bear in class to make my classmates laugh.’"
"There's something even more urgent!" Story Grandpa said. "My little Langlang, would you be willing to become... the successor of the storyteller?"
"Oh, I don't know if I can..."
"It's simple! I'll tell you many stories, and you must remember them all in your heart."
"I'm willing to try!"
Story Grandpa was too excited. He happily looked at the successor before him and cleared his throat.
"Kongte... Kongde... Kongti...
Kongda! Big and small, raise your ears!
Kongte... Kongde... Kongti... Kongda! My magical pocket has opened.
Let the story begin here..."

[P22] Until dawn, Story Grandpa told and told and told... 
Fables, fairy tales, myths, and legends flowed from his mouth like spring water. 
The little boy listened carefully, writing down every single word. 
Brush, brush, brush, the quill pen flew across the paper.

Story Grandpa first told him the fables of Aesop. 
"I love these stories so much!" the little Langlang said excitedly, 
"Do you know what I'm going to do? Hmm... to remember these 
stories, I've decided to write them all down!"

The task was completed. Camilodo, Carmen, and Berio slept peacefully.

[P23] One month later, the time that excited the little chicks arrived again. They all stared intently at the door.

There's nothing strange about it,
because today is Monday.

Monday……

Bang! Bang! Bang!

[P24] "Good evening, friends!
Tonight's gathering, first I'm going to tell you a story about a forest
singer and cheese lover who got tricked!"

This is...
The Crow and the Fox...
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《我要找到朗朗》的封面，展示了主角小鸡卡梅拉手持灯笼，与两只同伴在洞穴前探险的场景，背景中有一只巨大的熊，营造出紧张又充满冒险的氛围。
[P2] 这一页描绘了鸡舍里小鸡们在星期一到来前的紧张与期待：大部分小鸡兴奋躁动，而小卡门和伙伴们则安静等待，画面右侧小鸡们发出“咯！咯！咯！”的叫声，预示着即将发生的事件。
[P3] 故事爷爷来到鸡舍，小鸡们热情迎接。他坐下后，小鸡们安静下来，故事爷爷开始念魔法咒语，准备讲故事。
[P4] 本页通过三个画面展示了故事爷爷为小鸡们讲述的多个经典故事：列那狐的传奇、尤利西斯战胜独眼巨人，以及他们百听不厌的金鸡蛋故事，小鸡们听得入迷。
[P5] 故事爷爷结束讲故事，小鸡们依依不舍地送别他，并约定下周再来。卡门和卡梅利多送上他们画的画，表达感谢，画面展现了温馨的告别场景。
[P6] 小鸡们发现故事爷爷忘了带奶酪口袋，贝里奥偷吃了奶酪并被发现。故事爷爷在月光下疲惫地离开，感叹自己年老力衰，担忧未来无人为孩子们讲故事。
[P7] 小鸡们发现故事爷爷在哭泣，追上去后得知他因年老力衰、找不到接班人而悲伤，画面展现了故事爷爷在月光下痛哭的场景。
[P8] 故事爷爷在月光下遇到从井底出现的伊索叔叔的鬼魂，鬼魂告诉他未能找到继承者是件糟糕的事，并提醒他记住找到继承者的预言，预言指出继承者叫朗朗，藏在叶子上，需跟着箭头寻找。
[P9] 故事爷爷在月光下向小鸡们传达了伊索叔叔鬼魂的预言，要求他在三天内找到名为朗朗的继承者，否则故事将被遗忘。小鸡们听后深受触动，主动提出帮助他寻找继承者。
[P10] 小鸡们和故事爷爷踏上寻找继承者朗朗的旅程，故事爷爷由贝里奥背着前行，卡门提议跟着箭头走，卡梅利多询问故事的来源，故事爷爷解释故事多为代代相传的家族财富。
[P11] 小鸡们和故事爷爷来到短跑健将朗朗的家，希望他成为新的说书人。朗朗虽然热情，但记不住任何故事，甚至试图用打结的方式记住，结果引得大家捧腹大笑。
[P12] 小鸡们接连寻找了野兔、狼、猞猁和蜥蜴等名为朗朗的角色，但都不是预言中的继承者。卡门想出抬椅子的办法，大家第二天出发寻找山洞主人，却在洞口发现尸骨，贝里奥吓得不敢进入。
[P13] 小鸡们和故事爷爷在山洞深处发现一只正在熟睡的狗熊，他们轻声呼唤它，试图唤醒它，怀疑它就是预言中的继承者朗朗。
[P14] 小鸡们和故事爷爷在山洞中发现一只熟睡的狗熊，他们轻声唤醒它，发现它正是预言中名为朗朗的继承者。在卡梅利多的鼓励下，故事爷爷向狗熊朗朗提出成为说书人的请求，狗熊被惊醒后发出怒吼。
[P15] 小鸡们在山洞中发现熟睡的狗熊朗朗，它被小鸡拔出的箭头惊醒并大发雷霆。在得知箭头来历后，狗熊态度缓和，故事爷爷趁机请求它继承说书人职位，但狗熊因工作量大且需冬眠而婉拒，随即又睡着了。
[P16] 小鸡们在寻找预言中的朗朗时筋疲力尽，卡门想出用辘轳代替抬椅子的主意。他们决定最后一天去白鼬家寻找，同时农场里的人发现辘轳被偷，不知如何打水。
[P17] 小鸡们和故事爷爷在白鼬的洞口遇到自称是朗朗的白鼬，但其身上的臭味让众人难以忍受，故事爷爷甚至晕倒，贝里奥质疑其能否胜任说书人工作。
[P18] 小鸡们和故事爷爷继续寻找预言中的朗朗，他们询问了山洞里的熊、池塘边的青蛙以及獾，但这些自称朗朗的家伙都以各种理由拒绝接替说书人职位，最后在白鼬洞口遇到的白鼬也因臭味被嫌弃。
[P19] 小鸡们和故事爷爷在最后一天拜访猫头鹰朗朗未果，故事爷爷感到绝望。突然，卡梅利多发现木窗上钉着一支箭头，与之前射中狗熊朗朗的箭相同，众人兴奋地认为这是线索，呼喊贝里奥前来帮忙。
[P20] 小鸡们发现一个男孩在窗内熟睡，卡门认出他就是狗熊朗朗提到的预言中的朗朗，众人兴奋地冲进屋子，卡梅利多礼貌地询问男孩的名字。
[P21] 小鸡们和故事爷爷找到了预言中的朗朗——一个正在写检讨的男孩。男孩表示喜欢讲故事，愿意尝试接任说书人。故事爷爷激动地清了清嗓子，准备开始讲述第一个故事。
[P22] 故事爷爷为新找到的说书人小朗朗讲述伊索寓言，小朗朗兴奋地表示要将故事记录下来，众人完成任务后安心入睡。
[P23] 一个月后，小鸡们再次在星期一聚集，期待着什么，门被敲响，大家兴奋地迎接即将到来的活动。
[P24] 新任说书人小朗朗在夜晚的屋内，手持稿纸，向听众宣布要讲述一个关于森林里歌唱家和奶酪爱好者受骗的故事，并引出经典寓言《乌鸦与狐狸》。
